title: अध्याय ७४

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
राजाभूद् विख्यातः स्वराष्ट्रो नाम वीर्यवान् ।
अनेकयज्ञकृत् प्राज्ञः संग्रामेष्वपराजितः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
rājābhūd vikhyātaḥ svarāṣṭro nāma vīryavān |
anekayajñakṛt prājñaḥ saṃgrāmeṣvaparājitaḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
तस्यायुः सुमहत्प्रादात् मन्त्रिणाराधितो रविः ।
पत्नीनाञ्च शतन्तस्य धन्यानामभवद् द्विज ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
tasyāyuḥ sumahatprādāt mantriṇārādhito raviḥ |
patnīnāñca śatantasya dhanyānāmabhavad dvija || 2 ||

items.text:
तस्य दीर्घायुषः पत्न्यो नातिदीर्घायुषो मुने ।
कालेन जग्मुर्निधनं भृत्यमन्त्रिजनास्तथा ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
tasya dīrghāyuṣaḥ patnyo nātidīrghāyuṣo mune |
kālena jagmurnidhanaṃ bhṛtyamantrijanāstathā || 3 ||

items.text:
स भार्याभिस्तथायुक्तो भृत्यैश्च सहजन्मभिः ।
उद्विग्नचेताः संप्राप वीर्यहानिमहर्निशम् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
sa bhāryābhistathāyukto bhṛtyaiśca sahajanmabhiḥ |
udvignacetāḥ saṃprāpa vīryahānimaharniśam || 4 ||

items.text:
तं वीर्यहीनं निभृतैर्भृत्यैस्त्यक्तं सुदुः खितम् ।
अनन्तरो विमर्दाख्यो राज्याच्च्यावितवांस्तदा ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
taṃ vīryahīnaṃ nibhṛtairbhṛtyaistyaktaṃ suduḥ khitam |
anantaro vimardākhyo rājyāccyāvitavāṃstadā || 5 ||

items.text:
राज्याच्च्युतः सोऽपि वनं गत्वा निर्विण्णमानसः ।
तपस्तेपे महाभागे वितस्तापुलिने स्थितः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
rājyāccyutaḥ so'pi vanaṃ gatvā nirviṇṇamānasaḥ |
tapastepe mahābhāge vitastāpuline sthitaḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
ग्रीष्मे पञ्चतमा भूत्वा वर्षास्वभ्रंकषाशिकः ।
जलशायी च शिशिरे निराहारो यतव्रतः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
grīṣme pañcatamā bhūtvā varṣāsvabhraṃkaṣāśikaḥ |
jalaśāyī ca śiśire nirāhāro yatavrataḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
ततस्तपस्यतस्तस्य प्रावृट्काले महाप्लवः ।
बभूवानुदिनं मेघैर्वर्षद्भिरनुसन्ततम् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
tatastapasyatastasya prāvṛṭkāle mahāplavaḥ |
babhūvānudinaṃ meghairvarṣadbhiranusantatam || 8 ||

items.text:
न दिग्विज्ञायते पूर्वा दक्षिणा वा न पश्चिमा ।
नोत्तरा तमसा सर्वमनुलिप्तमिवाभवत् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
na digvijñāyate pūrvā dakṣiṇā vā na paścimā |
nottarā tamasā sarvamanuliptamivābhavat || 9 ||

items.text:
ततोऽतिपूरेण नृपः स नद्याः प्रेरितस्तटम् ।
प्रार्थयन्नापि नावाप ह्रियमाणो महीपतिः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
tato'tipūreṇa nṛpaḥ sa nadyāḥ preritastaṭam |
prārthayannāpi nāvāpa hriyamāṇo mahīpatiḥ || 10 ||

items.text:
अथ दूरे जलौघेन ह्रियमाणो महीपतिः ।
आससाद जले रौहीं स पुच्छे जगृहे च ताम् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
atha dūre jalaughena hriyamāṇo mahīpatiḥ |
āsasāda jale rauhīṃ sa pucche jagṛhe ca tām || 11 ||

items.text:
तेन प्लवेन स ययावूह्यमानो महीतले ।
इतश्चेतश्चान्धकारे आससाद तटन्ततः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
tena plavena sa yayāvūhyamāno mahītale |
itaścetaścāndhakāre āsasāda taṭantataḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
विस्तारि पङ्कमत्यर्थं दुस्तरं स नृपस्तरन् ।
तथैव कृष्यमाणोऽन्यद्रम्यं वनमवाप सः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
vistāri paṅkamatyarthaṃ dustaraṃ sa nṛpastaran |
tathaiva kṛṣyamāṇo'nyadramyaṃ vanamavāpa saḥ || 13 ||

items.text:
तत्रान्धकारे सा रौही चकर्ष वसुधाधिपम् ।
पुच्छे लग्नं महाभागं कृशं धमनिसन्ततौ ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
tatrāndhakāre sā rauhī cakarṣa vasudhādhipam |
pucche lagnaṃ mahābhāgaṃ kṛśaṃ dhamanisantatau || 14 ||

items.text:
तस्याश्च स्पर्शसंभूतामवापमुदमुत्तमाम् ।
सोऽन्धकारे भ्रमन् भूयो मदनाकृष्टमानसः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
tasyāśca sparśasaṃbhūtāmavāpamudamuttamām |
so'ndhakāre bhraman bhūyo madanākṛṣṭamānasaḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
विज्ञाय सानुरागं तं पृष्ठस्पर्शनतत्परम् ।
नरेन्द्रं तद्वनस्यान्तः सा मृगी तमुवाच ह ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
vijñāya sānurāgaṃ taṃ pṛṣṭhasparśanatatparam |
narendraṃ tadvanasyāntaḥ sā mṛgī tamuvāca ha || 16 ||

items.text:
किं पृष्ठं वेपथुमता करेण स्पृशसे मम ।
अन्यथैवास्य कार्यस्य सञ्जाता नृपते गतिः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
kiṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ vepathumatā kareṇa spṛśase mama |
anyathaivāsya kāryasya sañjātā nṛpate gatiḥ || 17 ||

items.text:
नास्थाने वो मनो यातं नागम्याहं तवेश्वर ।
किन्तु त्वत्सङ्गमे विघ्नमेष लोलः करोति मे ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
nāsthāne vo mano yātaṃ nāgamyāhaṃ taveśvara |
kintu tvatsaṅgame vighnameṣa lolaḥ karoti me || 18 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्या मृग्याश्च जगतीपतिः ।
जातकौतूहलो रौहीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
iti śrutvā vacastasyā mṛgyāśca jagatīpatiḥ |
jātakautūhalo rauhīmidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 19 ||

items.text:
का त्वं ब्रूहि मृगी वाक्यं कथं मानुषवद्वदेत् ।
कश्चैव लोलो यो विघ्नं त्वत्सङ्गे कुरुते मम ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
kā tvaṃ brūhi mṛgī vākyaṃ kathaṃ mānuṣavadvadet |
kaścaiva lolo yo vighnaṃ tvatsaṅge kurute mama || 20 ||

items.text:
अहन्ते दयिता भूप ! प्रागासमुत्पलावती ।
भार्या शताग्रमहिषी दुहिता दृढधन्वनः ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
ahante dayitā bhūpa ! prāgāsamutpalāvatī |
bhāryā śatāgramahiṣī duhitā dṛḍhadhanvanaḥ || 21 ||
items.speaker: मृग्युवाच

items.text:
राजोवाच
किन्तु यावत् कृतं कर्म येनेमां योनिमागता ।
पतिव्रता धर्मपरा सा चेत्थं कथमीदृशी ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
rājovāca
kintu yāvat kṛtaṃ karma yenemāṃ yonimāgatā |
pativratā dharmaparā sā cetthaṃ kathamīdṛśī || 22 ||

items.text:
अहं पितृगृहे बाला सखीभिः सहिता वनम् ।
रन्तुं गता ददर्शैकं मृगं मृग्या समागतम् ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
ahaṃ pitṛgṛhe bālā sakhībhiḥ sahitā vanam |
rantuṃ gatā dadarśaikaṃ mṛgaṃ mṛgyā samāgatam || 23 ||
items.speaker: मृग्युवाच

items.text:
ततः समीपवर्तिन्या मया सा ताडिता मृगी ।
मया त्रस्ता गतान्यत्र क्रुद्धः प्राह ततो मृगः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ samīpavartinyā mayā sā tāḍitā mṛgī |
mayā trastā gatānyatra kruddhaḥ prāha tato mṛgaḥ || 24 ||

items.text:
मूढे किमेवं मत्तासि धिक्ते दौःशील्यमीदृशम् ।
आधानकालो येनायं त्वया मे विफलीकृतः ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
mūḍhe kimevaṃ mattāsi dhikte dauḥśīlyamīdṛśam |
ādhānakālo yenāyaṃ tvayā me viphalīkṛtaḥ || 25 ||

items.text:
वाचं श्रुत्वा ततस्तस्य मानुषस्येव भाषतः ।
भीता तमब्रुवं कोऽसीत्येतां योनिमुपागतः ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
vācaṃ śrutvā tatastasya mānuṣasyeva bhāṣataḥ |
bhītā tamabruvaṃ ko'sītyetāṃ yonimupāgataḥ || 26 ||

items.text:
ततः स प्राह पुत्रोऽहमृषेर्निर्वृतिचक्षुषः ।
सुतपा नाम मृग्यान्तु साभिलाषो मृगोऽभवम् ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa prāha putro'hamṛṣernirvṛticakṣuṣaḥ |
sutapā nāma mṛgyāntu sābhilāṣo mṛgo'bhavam || 27 ||

items.text:
इमाञ्चानुगतः प्रेम्णा वाञ्छितश्चानया वने ।
त्वया वियोजिता दुष्टे तस्माच्छापं ददामि ते ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
imāñcānugataḥ premṇā vāñchitaścānayā vane |
tvayā viyojitā duṣṭe tasmācchāpaṃ dadāmi te || 28 ||

items.text:
मया चोक्तं तवाज्ञानादपराधः कृतो मुने ।
प्रसादं कुरु शापं मे न भवान् दातुमर्हति ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
mayā coktaṃ tavājñānādaparādhaḥ kṛto mune |
prasādaṃ kuru śāpaṃ me na bhavān dātumarhati || 29 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्तः प्राह मां सोऽपि मुनिरित्थं महीपते ।
न प्रयच्छामि शापं ते यद्यात्मानं ददासि मे ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
ityuktaḥ prāha māṃ so'pi muniritthaṃ mahīpate |
na prayacchāmi śāpaṃ te yadyātmānaṃ dadāsi me || 30 ||

items.text:
मया चोक्तं मृगी नाहं मृगरूपधरा वने ।
लप्स्यसेऽन्यां मृगीन्तावन्मयि भावो निवर्त्यताम् ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
mayā coktaṃ mṛgī nāhaṃ mṛgarūpadharā vane |
lapsyase'nyāṃ mṛgīntāvanmayi bhāvo nivartyatām || 31 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्तः कोपरक्ताक्षः स प्राह स्फुरिताधरः ।
नाहं मृगी त्वयेत्युक्तं मृगी मूढे भविष्यसि ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
ityuktaḥ koparaktākṣaḥ sa prāha sphuritādharaḥ |
nāhaṃ mṛgī tvayetyuktaṃ mṛgī mūḍhe bhaviṣyasi || 32 ||

items.text:
ततो भृशं प्रव्यथिता प्रणम्य मुनिमब्रुवम् ।
स्वरूपस्थमतिक्रुद्धं प्रसीदेति पुनः पुनः ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
tato bhṛśaṃ pravyathitā praṇamya munimabruvam |
svarūpasthamatikruddhaṃ prasīdeti punaḥ punaḥ || 33 ||

items.text:
बालानभिज्ञा वाक्यानां ततः प्रोक्तमिदं मया ।
पितर्यसति नारीभिर्व्रियते हि पतिः स्वयम् ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
bālānabhijñā vākyānāṃ tataḥ proktamidaṃ mayā |
pitaryasati nārībhirvriyate hi patiḥ svayam || 34 ||

items.text:
सति ताते कथञ्चाहं वृणोमि मुनिसत्तम ।
सापराधाथवा पादौ प्रसीदेश नमाम्यहम् ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
sati tāte kathañcāhaṃ vṛṇomi munisattama |
sāparādhāthavā pādau prasīdeśa namāmyaham || 35 ||

items.text:
प्रसीदेति प्रसीदेति प्रणताया महामते ।
इत्थं लालप्यमानायाः स प्राह मुनिपुङ्गवः ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
prasīdeti prasīdeti praṇatāyā mahāmate |
itthaṃ lālapyamānāyāḥ sa prāha munipuṅgavaḥ || 36 ||

items.text:
न भवत्यन्यथा प्रोक्तं मम वाक्यं कदाचन ।
मृगी भविष्यसि मृता वनेऽस्मिन्नेव जन्मनि ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
na bhavatyanyathā proktaṃ mama vākyaṃ kadācana |
mṛgī bhaviṣyasi mṛtā vane'sminneva janmani || 37 ||

items.text:
मृगत्वे च महाबाहुस्तव गर्भमुपैष्यति ।
लोलो नाम मुनेः पुत्रः सिद्धवीर्यस्य भामिनि ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
mṛgatve ca mahābāhustava garbhamupaiṣyati |
lolo nāma muneḥ putraḥ siddhavīryasya bhāmini || 38 ||

items.text:
जातिस्मरा भवित्री त्वं तस्मिन् गर्भमुपागते ।
स्मृतिं प्राप्य तथा वाचं मानुषीमीरयिष्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
jātismarā bhavitrī tvaṃ tasmin garbhamupāgate |
smṛtiṃ prāpya tathā vācaṃ mānuṣīmīrayiṣyasi || 39 ||

items.text:
तस्मिन् जाते मृगीत्वात् त्वं विमुक्ता पतिनार्चिता ।
लोकानवाप्स्यसि प्राप्या ये न दुष्कृतकर्मभिः ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
tasmin jāte mṛgītvāt tvaṃ vimuktā patinārcitā |
lokānavāpsyasi prāpyā ye na duṣkṛtakarmabhiḥ || 40 ||

items.text:
सोऽपि लोलो महावीर्यः पितृशत्रून् निपात्य वै ।
जित्वा वसुन्धरां कृत्स्त्रां भविष्यति ततो मनुः ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
so'pi lolo mahāvīryaḥ pitṛśatrūn nipātya vai |
jitvā vasundharāṃ kṛtstrāṃ bhaviṣyati tato manuḥ || 41 ||

items.text:
एवं शापमहं लब्ध्वा मृता तिर्यक्त्वमागता ।
त्वत्संस्पर्शाच्च गर्भोऽसौ संभूतो जठरे मम ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ śāpamahaṃ labdhvā mṛtā tiryaktvamāgatā |
tvatsaṃsparśācca garbho'sau saṃbhūto jaṭhare mama || 42 ||

items.text:
अतो ब्रवीमि नास्थाने तव यातं मनो मयि ।
न चाप्यगम्या गर्भस्थो लोलो विघ्नं करोत्यसौ ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
ato bravīmi nāsthāne tava yātaṃ mano mayi |
na cāpyagamyā garbhastho lolo vighnaṃ karotyasau || 43 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
एवमुक्तस्ततः सोऽपि राजा प्राप्य परां मुदम् ।
पुत्रो ममारीञ्जित्वेति पृथिव्यां भविता मनुः ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
evamuktastataḥ so'pi rājā prāpya parāṃ mudam |
putro mamārīñjitveti pṛthivyāṃ bhavitā manuḥ || 44 ||

items.text:
ततस्तं सुषुवे पुत्रं सा मृगी लक्षणान्वितम् ।
तस्मिन् जाते च भूतानि सर्वाणि प्रययुर्मुदम् ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr:
tatastaṃ suṣuve putraṃ sā mṛgī lakṣaṇānvitam |
tasmin jāte ca bhūtāni sarvāṇi prayayurmudam || 45 ||

items.text:
विशेषतश्च राजासौ पुत्रे जाते महाबले ।
सा विमुक्ता मृगी शापात् प्राप लोकाननुत्तमान् ॥ ४६ ॥
items.tr:
viśeṣataśca rājāsau putre jāte mahābale |
sā vimuktā mṛgī śāpāt prāpa lokānanuttamān || 46 ||

items.text:
ततस्तस्यर्षयः सर्वे समेत्य मुनिसत्तम ।
अवेक्ष्य भाविनीमृद्धिं नाम चक्रुर्महात्मनः ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr:
tatastasyarṣayaḥ sarve sametya munisattama |
avekṣya bhāvinīmṛddhiṃ nāma cakrurmahātmanaḥ || 47 ||

items.text:
तामसीं भजमानायां योनिं मातर्यजायत ।
तमसा चावृते लोके तामसोऽयं भविष्यति ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr:
tāmasīṃ bhajamānāyāṃ yoniṃ mātaryajāyata |
tamasā cāvṛte loke tāmaso'yaṃ bhaviṣyati || 48 ||

items.text:
ततः स तामसस्तेन पित्रा संवर्धितो वने ।
जातबुद्धिरुवाचेदं पितरं मुनिसत्तम ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sa tāmasastena pitrā saṃvardhito vane |
jātabuddhiruvācedaṃ pitaraṃ munisattama || 49 ||

items.text:
कस्त्वं तात कथं वाहं पुत्रो माता च का मम ।
किमर्थमागतश्च त्वमेतत् सत्यं ब्रवीहि मे ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr:
kastvaṃ tāta kathaṃ vāhaṃ putro mātā ca kā mama |
kimarthamāgataśca tvametat satyaṃ bravīhi me || 50 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
ततः पिता यथावृत्तं स्वराज्यच्यावनादिकम् ।
तस्याचष्टे महाबहुः पुत्रस्य जगतीपतिः ॥ ५१ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ pitā yathāvṛttaṃ svarājyacyāvanādikam |
tasyācaṣṭe mahābahuḥ putrasya jagatīpatiḥ || 51 ||

items.text:
श्रुत्वा तत् सकलं सोऽपि समाराध्य च भास्करम् ।
अवाप दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि ससंहाराण्यशेषतः ॥ ५२ ॥
items.tr:
śrutvā tat sakalaṃ so'pi samārādhya ca bhāskaram |
avāpa divyānyastrāṇi sasaṃhārāṇyaśeṣataḥ || 52 ||

items.text:
कृतास्त्रस्तानरीन् जित्वा पितुरानीय चान्तिकम् ।
अनुज्ञातान् मुनोचाथ तेन स्वं धर्ममास्थितः ॥ ५३ ॥
items.tr:
kṛtāstrastānarīn jitvā piturānīya cāntikam |
anujñātān munocātha tena svaṃ dharmamāsthitaḥ || 53 ||

items.text:
पितापि तस्य स्वान् लोकांस्तपोयज्ञसमार्जितान् ।
विसृष्टदेहः संप्राप्तो दृष्ट्वा पुत्रमुखं सुखम् ॥ ५४ ॥
items.tr:
pitāpi tasya svān lokāṃstapoyajñasamārjitān |
visṛṣṭadehaḥ saṃprāpto dṛṣṭvā putramukhaṃ sukham || 54 ||

items.text:
जित्वा समस्तां पृथिवीं तामसाख्यः स पार्थिवः ।
तामसाख्यो मनुरभूत्तस्य मन्वन्तरं शृणु ॥ ५५ ॥
items.tr:
jitvā samastāṃ pṛthivīṃ tāmasākhyaḥ sa pārthivaḥ |
tāmasākhyo manurabhūttasya manvantaraṃ śṛṇu || 55 ||

items.text:
ये देवा यत्पतिर्यश्च देवेन्द्रो ये तथर्षयः ।
ये पुत्राश्च मनोस्तस्य पृथिवीपरिपालकाः ॥ ५६ ॥
items.tr:
ye devā yatpatiryaśca devendro ye tatharṣayaḥ |
ye putrāśca manostasya pṛthivīparipālakāḥ || 56 ||

items.text:
सत्यास्तथान्ये सुधियः सुरूपा हरयस्तथा ।
एते देवगणास्तत्र सप्तविंशतिका मुने ॥ ५७ ॥
items.tr:
satyāstathānye sudhiyaḥ surūpā harayastathā |
ete devagaṇāstatra saptaviṃśatikā mune || 57 ||

items.text:
महाबलो महावीर्यः शतयज्ञोपलक्षितः ।
शिखिरिन्द्रस्तथा तेषां देवानामभवद्विभुः ॥ ५८ ॥
items.tr:
mahābalo mahāvīryaḥ śatayajñopalakṣitaḥ |
śikhirindrastathā teṣāṃ devānāmabhavadvibhuḥ || 58 ||

items.text:
ज्योतिर्धर्मा पृथुः काव्यश्चैत्रोऽग्निर्वलकस्तथा ।
पीवरश्च तथा ब्रह्मन् ! सप्त सप्तर्षयोऽभवन् ॥ ५९ ॥
items.tr:
jyotirdharmā pṛthuḥ kāvyaścaitro'gnirvalakastathā |
pīvaraśca tathā brahman ! sapta saptarṣayo'bhavan || 59 ||

items.text:
नरः क्षान्तिः शान्तदान्तजानुजङ्घादयस्तथा ।
पुत्रास्तु तामसस्यासन् राजानः सुमहाबलाः ॥ ६० ॥
items.tr:
naraḥ kṣāntiḥ śāntadāntajānujaṅghādayastathā |
putrāstu tāmasasyāsan rājānaḥ sumahābalāḥ || 60 ||

items.text:
इत्येतत्तामसं विप्र मन्वन्तरमुदाहृतम् ।
यः पठेत् शृणुयाद्वापि तमसा सन बाध्यते ॥ ६१ ॥
items.tr:
ityetattāmasaṃ vipra manvantaramudāhṛtam |
yaḥ paṭhet śṛṇuyādvāpi tamasā sana bādhyate || 61 ||

en_summary: Markandeya tells Kraushtuki of the birth of Tamasa, the fourth Manu. There was a famous, mighty king named Svarashtra, wise, the performer of many sacrifices and unbeaten in battle. The Sun, worshipped by his minister, gave him a very long life, and he had a hundred fine wives; but his wives did not live as long, and in time they died, as did his servants and ministers. Without his wives and the servants born with him, he grew troubled in mind and lost strength day and night. When he was weak and left by his servants, his neighbour (or rival) named Vimarda drove him from his kingdom. In despair he went to the forest and did penance on the bank of the Vitasta river: in summer amid five fires, in the rains under the open sky, in winter lying in water, fasting and keeping his vows. Then in the rainy season came a great flood, with clouds raining day after day; the directions could not be told apart and all seemed smeared with darkness. The swollen river swept him away from the bank; carried far by the water, he came upon a female deer (rohi) in the water and caught hold of her tail. Pulled along by her in the dark, he reached a bank, crossed a wide, deep stretch of mud and came to another lovely forest. The touch of the deer, as she dragged the thin king clinging to her tail, gave him great joy, and he became filled with desire. Seeing him eager and stroking her back, the deer spoke: why did he touch her back with a trembling hand? His heart had not gone to a wrong place, and she was not forbidden to him, but this Lola was blocking their union. Curious, the king asked who she was, how a deer could speak like a human, and who this Lola was. She said she had once been his beloved Utpalavati, the chief of his hundred queens, daughter of Dridhadhanvan. Asked what deed had brought her, a faithful and dutiful wife, to this birth, she explained: as a girl in her father's house she went to the forest with friends and saw a male deer with a doe; she struck the doe, which ran away in fright. The male deer angrily scolded her for ruining his time for begetting young, and she, afraid at hearing him speak like a man, asked who he was. He was Sutapas, son of the sage Nirvritichakshus, who had become a deer out of desire for the doe; since she had parted them he would curse her, unless she gave herself to him. She refused, saying she was no doe and he could find another. In anger he said that since she had said 'I am not a doe', she would become a doe. She begged him again and again, saying she was a young girl who did not know how to speak, and that a woman chooses a husband herself only when her father is not alive. He said his word never fails: after death, in this same forest, she would become a doe; while a deer she would carry in her womb the mighty Lola, son of the sage Siddhavirya; when he entered her womb she would remember her past life and speak human speech; when he was born she would be freed from the deer state, honoured by her husband, and reach worlds evil-doers cannot reach; and Lola would kill his father's enemies, conquer the whole earth and become a Manu. So, she said, she had died and become an animal, and from the king's touch this child had been conceived in her; Lola in the womb was the obstacle. The king rejoiced that his son would conquer his enemies and become a Manu. The doe gave birth to a son with all good marks; all beings, and the king above all, rejoiced, and she, freed from the curse, reached the highest worlds. The assembled sages, foreseeing his future greatness, named him Tamasa, because he was born while his mother was in a dark (tamasi) birth and the world was covered in darkness (tamas). Raised by his father in the forest, when he grew up he asked who his father was, how he was his son and who his mother was. His father told him everything, from the loss of the kingdom on. Tamasa worshipped the Sun and received all the divine weapons with the means of withdrawing them, defeated his father's enemies, brought them before his father, released them with his permission and kept to his own duty. His father, having seen his son's face with joy, left his body and reached the worlds earned by his penance and sacrifices. Tamasa conquered the whole earth and became the Manu Tamasa. In his period the gods were the Satyas, Sudhis, Surupas and Haris, groups of twenty-seven; their lord, the Indra, was Shikhi, mighty and marked by a hundred sacrifices. The seven sages were Jyotirdharma, Prithu, Kavya, Chaitra, Agni, Valaka and Pivara. The sons of Tamasa, very strong kings, were Nara, Kshanti, Shanta, Danta, Janu, Jangha and others. Whoever reads or hears of the Tamasa period is not troubled by darkness (tamas).
